title: Put cheap PR eligibility guards in the job-level `if`, not in shell steps, in community-label.yml
answers: community label job runs for bot or maintainer PRs
skip community labeling before runner is allocated
why does the community-label workflow still provision a runner for member PRs
where to add an exclusion for internal authors in community-label workflow
body:
Symptom: Bot-authored and maintainer (MEMBER/COLLABORATOR/OWNER) PRs still queue a labeling job and get a runner, even though the labeling is skipped.
Root cause: .github/workflows/community-label.yml:label-community had only `github.repository == 'mlflow/mlflow'` as its job `if`; the bot and association checks ran as shell `exit 0` inside the `run:` step, after runner allocation.
Fix pattern: Express static, payload-only eligibility checks (user.type != 'Bot', author_association not in the internal list) in the job-level `if:` expression, using `fromJSON('[...]')` with `contains(...)` for the association list. Delete the matching shell guards and their env vars (AUTHOR_TYPE, ASSOCIATION).
Constraints: Only checks that need no API call belong in `if:`. The profile (company/email Databricks) and commit-email affiliation checks need `gh api` and stay in the script step. Applies to this workflow's job condition; other workflows may differ.
applies: Edits to .github/workflows/community-label.yml job conditions and steps; any workflow where skip decisions use only event payload fields.
says: Community labeling jobs allocate and waste build runners on pull requests submitted by maintainers.
Automated bot pull requests spin up build machines just to immediately skip labeling.
Skip community contributor label checks before reserving a runner when internal team members create PRs.
Prevent community labeling workflows from queuing jobs whenever bots or project collaborators push branches.
search: Job conditions in .github/workflows/community-label.yml must use the job-level if expression for static, payload-only eligibility checks to avoid allocating a runner for bot or maintainer pull requests. Checks such as user.type != 'Bot' and author_association not in the internal list using fromJSON and contains belong in if:, replacing shell exit 0 guards and AUTHOR_TYPE and ASSOCIATION environment variables. Checks requiring gh api calls, such as company and commit-email affiliations, must remain inside the script step.
